symptom.disease_name: Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

sampled_features.disease_name: Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

additional_requirements: delusions_and_hallucinations occur exclusively during the major depressive episode

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: The feeling that one is useless and has no value.
subtypes.Ruminative Guilt: A thought pattern of obsessively replaying past minor mistakes or flaws and constantly reproaching oneself.
subtypes.Excessive or Inappropriate Guilt: Feeling excessive responsibility for trivial matters or daily events and believing one deserves punishment.
subtypes.Delusional Guilt: Guilt reaching a delusional level, disconnected from reality, involving feeling responsible for unrelated unfortunate events.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.

subtypes.Reduced Concentration: Unable to pay attention or maintain focus on specific activities like conversation, reading, or watching TV.
subtypes.Indecisiveness: Extreme difficulty making even minor daily choices (e.g., menu, clothes) and hesitating to make decisions.
subtypes.Subjective Memory Complaints: Complaining of memory decline, such as forgetting where things were placed, due to reduced focus.
subtypes.Clouded Thinking: Thinking feels foggy, dazed, or not clear.

symptom.disease_info: Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features is characterized by one or more major depressive episodes accompanied by delusions and/or hallucinations that occur exclusively during these depressive episodes. The psychotic content is often mood-congruent, involving themes of guilt, worthlessness, illness, or deserved punishment, and is typically less systematized than in primary psychotic disorders. Clinically, it tends to present with more severe functional impairment, higher suicide risk, and greater psychomotor and cognitive slowing than non-psychotic depression, and may have a recurrent course. It is distinguished from schizoaffective disorder and schizophrenia by the absence of psychotic symptoms outside of mood episodes and by the temporal alignment between mood disturbance and psychosis.

patient.personality: Aaron is a warm, routine-loving caregiver who thrives on community connections and simple pleasures but can be laid-back and disorganized about his own obligations.
patient.stressor: Over the past year, Aaron’s hours at the home-care agency were repeatedly cut as several long-term clients were moved to assisted living, leaving him juggling part-time shifts at different sites and falling behind on rent and bills. His easygoing attitude toward paperwork and money, which had never caused more than minor hassles before, suddenly led to overdraft fees, collection calls, and the real possibility of eviction, which he experienced as a humiliating failure given his reputation as a dependable aide and church volunteer. As the financial pressure mounted, he began skipping social activities and fishing trips to take every available shift, yet still watched his debts grow, and he grew increasingly withdrawn and preoccupied with the idea that he was being judged and quietly talked about by neighbors and coworkers. After about two months of this decline, he finally came to psychiatric care at the urging of his pastor and a supervisor, who were alarmed by his dramatic weight loss, inability to keep up with simple tasks, and his insistence that his financial problems were a sign that God and the community had turned against him.
patient.chief_complaint: “I’ve dropped so much weight without trying, and I just don’t feel like eating anymore.”

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: Lately I’m convinced that my money troubles aren’t just bad luck—that God and the people at church have decided I’m no good and are quietly making sure I lose my clients and end up on the street because I deserve to be punished for messing up so badly with my bills.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.
S025.manifestation: I used to look forward to fishing on Saturdays and joking around with the folks at church, but now even on my days off I just sit in my apartment staring at the wall because nothing, not even seeing my friends or my grandnieces, feels like it’s worth getting dressed for anymore.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.
S026.manifestation: I pretty much force down a piece of toast or a few crackers so I don’t pass out at work, but most days my stomach feels knotted up and the thought of real food just makes me feel sick, and my clothes are hanging off me now even though I haven’t tried to diet or anything.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: Most nights I lie in bed for hours with my mind stuck on the bills and this feeling that everyone’s turned against me, and when I do finally doze off I’m up again at three or four in the morning, staring at the ceiling and dreading the day because I know I won’t get back to sleep.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.
S029.manifestation: Even on days when I don’t have many clients, just taking a shower, packing my lunch, and walking to the bus feels like I’ve run a marathon, and by the time I get home I’m so wiped out I can barely stand long enough to heat up a can of soup.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).
S030.manifestation: I walk into my clients’ homes and feel like a complete fraud, like I’m pretending to be this caring, dependable aide when deep down I’m rotten and selfish, and I keep thinking all these money problems are proof that I’ve let everyone down and ought to lose everything I have.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.
S031.manifestation: At work now I find myself standing in the kitchen trying to remember if I already gave Mrs. L her morning pills, and even simple things like filling out my time sheet or deciding which bill to pay first can leave me frozen and staring at the paper for fifteen minutes because my brain just won’t sort it out.
